subject: Private Deployment: patch tranche sequencing & NOC drill schedule
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private Deployment: patch tranche sequencing & NOC drill schedule

Team —

We need to lock down the patch tranche plan and schedule a NOC drill for Acme's private deployment (VPC regions: us-west-2). Goals: minimal customer impact, certified rollback rehearsals, and artifact verification. High-level proposal attached (patch_tranche_matrix_v2.xlsx). Key points: 

- Tranche approach: 4 tranches, each ~8-10% of capacity; can increase to 12% if health checks pass.
- Maintenance windows: 00:30–03:30 PDT (preferred) for tranche runs; Acme asked to avoid 12:00–14:00 local ops hours.
- Version pinning: only pin-to-release X.Y.Z+1 for the initial canary tranche; full roll uses X.Y.Z+2 after canary green.
- Rollback: automated unpin and node-replacement path; manual evacuation if KV cache mismatch observed.

Asks: 
1) Karthik — confirm drain/evacuation steps and expected per-node drain time.
2) Soojin — prepare a short rollback rehearsal script we can run in the dry-run and attach to the runbook.
3) Monica — coordinate NOC invites and make sure Alerting runbooks are in the incident channel.
4) Acme Ops — confirm blackout windows and whether you can accept 10% capacity offline during canary.

Attachments: patch_tranche_matrix_v2.xlsx; I also linked a working folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PrivateUpgradePrep

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: soojin.lee@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, ops@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-10-03T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Deployment: patch tranche sequencing & NOC drill schedule

Naomi —

Thanks for the plan. Quick technical points and asks: 

- Drain/evacuate: expected median drain time per GPU node is ~95s for idle traffic; under KV-heavy chat workloads plan for up to 4.5 minutes. We should add a 6-minute buffer in the tranche window for node replacement.
- KV cache syncronization: if cache mismatch occurs after a patch we should run immediate roll-forward with the same quantized artifact OR perform a rolling kv-warm step (see step 4 in my attached checklist).
- Network quiesce: we'll coordinate BGP prep — we should avoid doing tranche 3 and 4 across the same Top-of-Rack to reduce blast radius.

I attached a small rollback checklist (rollback-checklist.txt) with the commands and the audit steps. Suggestion: run a canary with 2 pods first, then escalate if telemetry is green for 15 minutes.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Serving Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: rollback-checklist.txt

Date: 2026-10-04T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Deployment: patch tranche sequencing & NOC drill schedule

Naomi / team —

Thanks for the outline. A few constraints from Acme SRE side: 

- We cannot take more than 10% of production capacity offline during business hours. Canary window OK overnight as requested, but local ops want the 12:00–14:00 window protected (no maintenance).
- We'll provide SHA256 checksums for all artifacts 24 hours before each tranche.
- Our monitoring only keeps fine-grain request tracing for 72 hours — please ensure any debug artifacts are collected in the 24–72 hour window post-tranche.

We can support the NOC dry-run the week of Oct 12; suggest 2026-10-13 00:30 PDT for the rehearsal (canary + rollback). We'll have our on-call (me + 1 SRE) in the channel.

-Jorge
Jorge Martinez

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-10-05T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Deployment: patch tranche sequencing & NOC drill schedule

Naomi / all —

Draft rollback rehearsal plan (summary):

1) Preflight (T-24h): artifact SIGs + smoke test results uploaded to shared folder.
2) Canary run (T0): deploy to 2 pods (~8% capacity), run traffic ramp to 25% of normal to stress KV paths. Monitor: 1min P99 latency, error-rate, memory pressure.
3) Abort criteria: P99 > 2x baseline for 5 continuous minutes OR error-rate > 0.5% sustained for 3 minutes. If abort triggered -> execute automated unpin + node-replace; run KV-warm step after replacement.
4) Manual rollback drill (if canary fails): run the manual evacuation checklist (attached in rollback-checklist.txt), confirm artifact re-deployment and telemetry back to baseline for 15 minutes.
5) Postmortem stub (T+3h): collect traces and submit initial findings to JIRA OPS-1427.

Circuit breaker specifics: add a temporary routing rule to divert 10% traffic to fallback model variant for 30 minutes if metrics cross thresholds. This gives breathing room for node-replacement without affecting all customers.

I put the rehearsal agenda into noc_dryrun_agenda.pdf and referenced the runbook in the shared drive. Suggest we run the dry-run on Oct 13 as Acme proposed and schedule a follow-up on Oct 14 to review telemetry.

-Soojin
Soojin Lee
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private Deployment: patch tranche sequencing & NOC drill schedule

All —

Thanks for the fast responses and the checklist. Final schedule and action items: 

- Dry-run (canary + rollback rehearsal): 2026-10-13 00:30–02:00 PDT — confirmed with Acme. Monica to send calendar invites by EOD 2026-10-07.
- Artifacts: release X.Y.Z+1 (canary) SHA256 to be uploaded by 2026-10-12 00:30. Acme will post checksums.
- Karthik: add the 6-minute drain buffer to the tranche matrix and call out KV-warm step ordering.
- Soojin: run the NOC drill script during dry-run; record the session and drop notes in the shared drive.
- Monica: ensure incident channels are prepared and that on-call rotation for Oct 13 is staffed.

I'll update JIRA OPS-1427 with this schedule and the runbook links. Please confirm here once invites and artifact uploads are complete.

Thanks — feeling good about this plan. Keep the comments coming if we need to tighten thresholds.

Naomi Feldman
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
